299:
The personnel policies and procedures of the county in effect on December 19, 1995, shall continue in effect after such date, such to any amendments, restatements or replacements of the personnel policies and procedures adopted by the board of commissioners. The personnel policies and procedures shall cover, but shall not be limited to, the following:
(1) The preparation, maintenance and revision of a position classification plan for all regular employment positions covered by this chapter, based upon similarity of duties performed and responsibilities assumed, so that such qualifications may reasonably be required for, and that the schedule of pay may be equitably applied to, all positions in the same class. After such classification plan has been approved by the board of commissioners, the human resources manager shall allocate or reallocate the position of every employee covered by this chapter to one of the classes in the plan. Any employee affected by the allocation or reallocation of a position to a class shall, after filing with the human resources manager a form as the human resources manager may prescribe, be given a reasonable opportunity to be heard thereon.
(2) The establishment of a compensation plan for all county employees.
(3) The recruitment of capable persons and for administering of fair and open evaluations, to determine the relative fitness of applicants for positions with the county.
(4) The certification to the appointing authority of the names of persons who are categorized as qualified to fill a vacancy with the county.
(5) The establishment and maintenance of eligible lists for appointments and promotions.
(6) The method for promotions which shall give appropriate consideration to the applicant's qualifications, record of performance and ability.
(7) Upon appointment or promotion, a period of employee probation, not to exceed one year. If an employee is terminated during such probationary period, the employee shall not be entitled to the grievance procedures established for regular employment positions.
(8) The establishment of programs, including trainee programs, designed to attract and utilize persons with minimal qualifications, but with potential for development, in order to provide career development opportunities among members of disadvantaged groups, handicapped persons and returning veterans. Such programs may provide for appointment upon the satisfactory completion of the training period without further examination.
(9) The keeping of records of the performance of all employees covered by this chapter, which performance records shall be considered in determining salary increments or increases for meritorious services; as a factor in promotions; as a factor in determining the order of layoffs because of lack of funds or work and in reinstatement; and as a factor in demotions, discharges and transfers.
(10) Provisions for layoffs by reason of lack of funds or work, or abolition of a position, or material change in duties or organization, and for reemployment of employees so laid off.
(11) The establishment of a plan and procedures for resolving grievances and complaints and the procedures for hearings and appeals in connection with such grievances and complaints, which shall include the provisions set forth in section 2-368(2). Such measures shall provide for presentation of charges, hearing rights and appeals for all permanent employees in the career service.
(12) The establishment of hours of work, holidays and attendance regulations in various classes of positions in the career service.
(13) The establishment of fringe benefits, such as insurance programs, retirement and leave policies.
(14) The development and operation of programs to improve work effectiveness, including training, safety, health, welfare, counseling, recreation and employee relations.
(15) Such other policies and administrative regulations, not inconsistent with this chapter, as may be proper and necessary for the enforcement of this chapter.
(Code 1979, § 2-11-10; Ord. No. 95-6, § 2, 12-19-1995)

The civil service commission shall perform the following duties and responsibilities.
(1) Provide input and make recommendations on all current or proposed policies and procedures. The comments and recommendations of the commission on such matters shall be considered by the board of commissioners when policies are presented.
(2) Hear the appeals of grievances under the then current county personnel policies and procedures which the county staff and the employee have not been able to resolve. At such hearing, the parties may present evidence relevant to the issues being considered; however, the technical rules of evidence shall not apply. Relevant evidence shall be any evidence that a reasonable person would consider in seeking to rule on the issues presented, as determined by the civil service commission. All testimony shall be under oath or affirmation. A record of the proceeding shall be made by tape recording or court reporter. If the decision of the commission is appealed, a written transcript of the record shall be prepared. The commission shall render its findings in a written report to be submitted to the parties to the grievance in not more than three business days following the day of the conclusion of the hearing. Either party to the grievance may appeal the findings of the commission to the board of commissioners in accordance with procedures for such appeal set out in the current county personnel policies and procedures. The appeal to the board of commissioners shall be based on the record of the proceeding before the commission and no evidence shall be presented to the board of commissioners, unless the board of commissioners shall make a finding that the evidence was not available at the time of the hearing before the commission or could not have been discovered at that time with the exercise of due diligence and agrees to allow the submission of the specified evidence.
(Code 1979, § 2-11-8; Ord. No. 95-6, § 2, 12-19-1995; Ord. No. 17-08, § 14(Exh. N), 2-6-2018)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl or spirits of wine, from whatever source or by whatever process produced.
Alcoholic beverage means and includes all drinks or beverages containing alcohol, including, but not limited to, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine or fortified wine.
Alcoholic treatment facility means any alcohol treatment facility owned and operated by the state or county, including the buildings and the surrounding property or campus directly incorporated into such use.
Beer or malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than 14 percent alcohol by volume, and including but not limited to ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small/low-alcohol beer and strong beer. The terms do not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Board of commissioners means the Board of Commissioners of Columbia County.
Church building means the main structure used by any religious organization for purposes of worship and the surrounding property or campus directly incorporated into such use in compliance with the zoning ordinances of the county.
County park or playground means a park, recreation center, ball fields or playgrounds owned and operated by the county for use by the citizens of the county.
Distilled spirits or spirituous liquor means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 24 percent alcohol by volume, including, but not limited to, all fortified wines.
Eating establishment means a business establishment which sells prepared food for consumption on the premises, with a full service kitchen offering food service every hour such establishment is open, and deriving at least 50 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared food items which shall not include the sale of any alcoholic beverages. An eating establishment which was in operation on January 1, 1992, possessed a county business license at that time, and has been in continuous operation since January 1, 1992, must have its full service kitchen approved by the health department and the development services division. Any other eating establishment must have its full service kitchen approved by the health department, development services division and the fire marshal where state law requires the establishment to be inspected by the fire marshal.
Fortified wine means any alcoholic beverage made from fruits, berries or grapes, containing more than 24 percent alcohol by volume, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes, but is not limited to, brandy.
Full service kitchen means a kitchen that must contain at least a three-compartment pot sink, a commercial grade stove or grill and oven which is permanently installed, and a commercial grade cooler or refrigerator. The full service kitchen must be approved by the health department, development services division, and the fire marshal, where State law requires the establishment to be inspected by the fire marshal.
Governing authority means the Board of Commissioners of Columbia County.
Growler means a glass bottle not to exceed 64 ounces that is filled by a licensee or employee of the licensed establishment with beer from a keg.
Hotel means a business establishment, which provides sleeping accommodations for rent, either on a transient or permanent residence basis, either maintaining a minimum of 50 rooms available for rent and having one or more dining rooms with kitchen facilities as required for an eating establishment, or maintaining less than 50 rooms, but at least three rooms which are available for rent, having at least one dining room with kitchen facilities as required for an eating establishment, and deriving gross sales from the sale of prepared food items in an amount exceeding its gross sales from the sale of alcoholic beverages. A motel meeting the qualifications set out in this definition shall be deemed a hotel. A hotel may grant a franchise or lease to a third party for the operation of an establishment pursuant to a license within the hotel, and such establishment shall still be treated as part of the hotel.
Indoor commercial recreational establishment means a business establishment which regularly serves prepared food from a full service kitchen during every hour it is open for business, and which derives at least 70 percent of its total annual gross sales from sales of prepared food and other goods and services other than alcoholic beverages, with the sale of alcoholic beverages being incidental to the establishment's primary business activity at the location. The primary business activity shall be offering a recreational activity such as, but not limited to, dinner theaters, bowling centers, bingo parlors, billiard parlors and other similar activities. Outdoor recreational activities, dance halls, nightclubs, taverns, video arcades, skating arenas, adult entertainment and/or sexually related entertainment and similar activities are specifically excluded from this definition.
License means a license for the sale of alcoholic beverages issued pursuant to the terms of this chapter.
Licensee means the person to whom a license under this chapter is issued.
Liter means the metric measurement of volume currently used by the United States.
Main entrance door means the principal entrance by which access may be obtained to the operational area of a structure. In the case of a county park or playground or other similar facility which does not have a principal entrance to a structure, this term shall mean the main entrance gate to the facility.
Operating manager means an individual with primary responsibility of the day to day operations of the business for which the license is sought and is neither an owner nor officer of the licensee, partnership, corporation or other business entity.
Outdoor commercial recreational establishment means a business establishment, the primary business of which is offering outdoor recreational activities and/or outdoor sports spectator activities to members of the public or members of the establishment if it is a private club, and which regularly serves prepared food from a full service kitchen during every hour in which it is open for business, and which derives at least 70 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of its recreational activities, sports spectator activities, prepared food and other goods and services other than alcoholic beverages, with the sale of alcoholic beverages being incidental to the establishment's primary business activity at that location. Establishments that are on a commercial vessel operating or moored in waters located within Columbia County are exempt from the full-service kitchen requirement. The primary business activity shall be offering an outdoor recreational activity or sports spectator activity such as, but not limited to, golf courses, golf training centers and/or driving ranges, tennis facilities, swimming facilities, automobile race tracks, fishing facilities and other similar activities. Adult entertainment and/or sexual entertainment facilities are specifically excluded from this definition.
Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel or other original consumer container.
Premises means a physically identifiable place of business of one or more contiguous rooms, operating under the same trade name, where alcoholic beverages are sold. In hotels and private clubs, the premises shall include eating areas, ballrooms, meeting facilities, reception rooms, guest rooms and patio areas of such hotel or private club located within the boundaries of the land on which such hotel or private club is built.
Private club means any nonprofit corporation or nonprofit association organized under the laws of this state which:
(1) Has been in existence at least one year prior to filing an application for a license;
(2) Has at least 75 regular dues-paying members; and
(3) Owns, hires or leases a building or space within a building for the reasonable use of its members, which building or space:
a. Has full service kitchen and dining room space and equipment;
b. Is staffed with a sufficient number of employees for cooking, preparing and serving meals for its members and guests; and
c. Has no member, officer, agent or employee directly or indirectly receiving, in the form of salary or other compensation, any profits for the sale of alcoholic beverages beyond a "fixed salary," as such term is defined in O.C.G.A. § 3-7-1, as amended from time to time.

School building means only the state, county or church school buildings and buildings at other schools in which are taught subjects commonly taught in the common schools and colleges of the state and the surrounding property or campus which is directly incorporated into such uses, provided that schools other than state or county schools must be in compliance with the county zoning ordinances.
Wholesaler or wholesale dealer means any person holding the appropriate license who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail package dealers or to retail consumption dealers.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage made from fruits, berries or grapes which contain not more than 21 percent alcohol, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. This term includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, sake, rectified wines, etc. This term does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at the point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to this definition.
Wine or beer tasting means a special event where wine or beer sampling can occur, typically when a customer requests a sample of a wine or beer offered for sale within the premises, or in conjunction with wine education classes, and sampling designed to promote wine appreciation and education, or as a nonprofit fundraiser.

If the application is denied, the board of commissioners or its designated committee shall set forth the reasons for the denial.
(h) In all instances in which an application is denied under the provisions of this article, the applicant, or related person or entity, may not reapply for a similar license for the same location for at least one year from the date of such denial.
(i) In the event multiple applications are submitted for a license permitting the sale of distilled spirits in packages and the proposed locations are within one mile of each other, the first complete application, as determined by the director of development services or designee, shall be considered until a determination of whether the application is denied or granted and any appeal rights with respect to such application has been exhausted.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 22-02, § 1(Exh. A), 5-17-2022)
349:
Any application for a license made pursuant to this article may be withdrawn by the applicant at any time. If the application is withdrawn before the license is issued, any sums deposited as license fees will be refunded. After issuance of a license, no refunds will be made. No refunds shall be made under any circumstances for investigation and administrative fees required in this article.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
350:
(a) Citizenship; residency. A license will be issued only to a person who is a citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence in the United States. Where an applicant is other than a natural person, it must be an entity organized and existing under the laws of the United States or one of its states, an agent of the entity must meet the qualifications set forth herein.
(1) Where the applicant for a license is an entity other than a natural person, the application shall be made jointly in the name of the entity and an officer having authority to bind the entity. Said entity shall be registered to do business in the State of Georgia.
(2) Licenses issued to entities must be issued jointly to the entity and all of the other persons required by this section to join in the application. All respective partners, officers, directors, or members, as applicable, shall be responsible for the actions of the named licensee and the conduct of the licensed business.
(b) Operation of business. If none of the applicants required above have primary responsibility of the day to day operations of the business for which the license is sought, then the operating manager shall join in the application. All persons named on the application shall be deemed "applicants".
(c) Background check. The person who has the primary responsibilities of the day to day operations of the business for which the license is sought shall submit a personnel statement in the form prescribed by the director of development services, and submit to a background check.
(d) Moral character; criminal record. No person or entity shall be granted an alcoholic beverage license unless it shall appear to the satisfaction of the commission that such persons or partners in the firms or officers and directors of the company shall be of good moral character.
(e) Age. An applicant must be 21 years of age or older.
(f) Interest in business; involvement in business. An applicant must have a bona-fide interest in the business for which the license is sought.
(g) Eligibility. The following individuals are not eligible for an alcoholic beverage license, even if they possess all of the qualifications listed herein.
(1) Any person convicted of a felony within the ten years immediately preceding the date of receipt of submission of the application.
(2) Any person convicted of a misdemeanor within the five years immediately preceding the date of receipt of submission of the application
(3) Any person who has been convicted of a crime of moral turpitude or gambling within ten years immediately preceding the date of receipt of submission of the application.
(4) Any person whose license to sell alcoholic beverages has been revoked for cause in any county, municipality, state or territory of the United States within the ten years preceding the filing of the application.
(5) Any person who has knowingly falsified information or made any material misrepresentation on the application for a license under this chapter or any application under the predecessor ordinance for Columbia County submitted within the ten years preceding the filing of the application.
(6) Any person who has been convicted of a violation of any federal, state or local law pertaining to the possession, manufacture, or sale of alcoholic beverages, controlled substances, or imitation controlled substances within the ten years preceding the filing of the application.
(7) Should any such applicant, partner or officer or director of any applicant entity, after a license has been granted, be convicted or plead guilty or nolo contendere to a crime involving moral turpitude, or to the violation of any laws of the State of Georgia regulating possession or the sale of controlled substances, imitation controlled substances, drugs, liquors, wine or beer or the lottery laws of this state, said license shall be subject after hearing to immediate suspension or revocation. Should the operating manager be convicted or plead guilty or nolo contendere to a crime involving moral turpitude, or to the violation of any laws of the State of Georgia regulating possession or the sale of narcotics, drugs, liquors, wine or beer or the lottery laws of this state, the licensee shall have seven days to report to the director of development services and any such violation 45 days from such conviction to revise its license to add a new operating manager. Failure to report a violation within the time prescribed shall automatically revoke applicant's license.
(h) Surrogates. The board of commissioners or its designated committee may decline to issue a license under this article when any person having any ownership interest in or any control over the land or building in which the establishment to be operated pursuant to the license will be located, or where any person who has control over the operation of the establishment, does not meet the same character requirements as set forth in this section for the licensee.
(i) Registered agent. Applicant must appoint and continuously maintain in the county a registered agent upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this article may be served. The registered agent must be a resident of the county. The licensee shall file the name of such registered agent, along with the written consent to serve of such agent, with the director of development services.
(j) Extenuating circumstances. The board of commissioners or its designated committee, in its discretion, may consider any extenuating circumstances which may reflect favorably or unfavorably on the applicant, the application or the proposed location of the establishment. If, in the board of commissioners' or the committee's judgment, circumstances are such that issuing of a license under this article would not be in the best interest of the general public, such circumstances may be grounds for denying the application.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 19-07, § 1(Exh. A), 4-2-2019)
351:
A person filing an application for a new license under this article as opposed to an application for the renewal of an existing license shall give public notice of the filing of the application as follows:
(1) By publishing a notice of the application in the newspaper in which sheriff's sales in the county are placed, in a form approved by the director of development services, three times in the 30 days preceding the consideration of the application by the board of commissioners;
(2) By posting a sign for at least 30 days preceding the consideration of the application by the board of commissioners in a prominent position on the property where it can be readily read from the road, which states:
"Application has been made to the board of commissioners for a license to sell (beer) (wine) (distilled spirits) for consumption (on) (off) premises at this location."
Date:________ ___________ Name of Applicant
The applicant must provide the board of commissioners proof of the giving of such public notice at or prior to the board of commissioners' consideration of the application.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
352:
(a) No establishment, with the exception of retail package sales of distilled spirits for off-premise consumption, operated pursuant to a license under this article shall be located in a building which is closer than 600 feet to a church building, a school building, county park or playground, or an alcoholic treatment facility. In applying this section, the director of development services or designee, shall determine what property is included in a school building, church building, county park or playground, or alcoholic treatment facility.
(b) For purposes of this section, subject to the qualifications set forth in this subsection, distances shall be measured in a straight line from the main entrance door of the establishment for which the license under this article is being sought to the nearest point on the boundary line of the land making up the campus of the church building, school building, county park or playground, or alcoholic treatment facility.
(c) No establishment which is being operated pursuant to a county license to sell alcohol on May 19, 2015, the effective date of this article, shall be denied continued operation under such existing license, nor denied any renewal of such license, nor shall any new owner of such establishment be denied a new license based upon the measurements set forth in this section. Upon cessation of the operation of the establishment as set forth in section 6-56 pursuant to such license, such exemption shall cease. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the cessation of the operation of the establishment is for one year or less, such exemption shall not cease.
(d) The holder of title to any property making up a church building, school building, county park or playground, or alcoholic treatment facility may waive the distance requirements of this section as they apply to such facility in any specific instance by recording in the real estate records in the office of the clerk of superior court of the county, a written instrument evidencing such waiver and setting out the terms thereof, which instrument shall be executed and witnessed with the same formalities as a deed filed for record in the clerk's office.
(e) This section shall not apply within the area of the county bounded on the west by Evans Town Center Blvd, on the north and east by North Belair Road, and on the south by Evans to Locks Road.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 18-03, § 1(Exh. A), 2-6-2018; Ord. No. 22-02, § 1(Exh. A), 5-17-2022)
353:
(a) Upon making application for a license under this article, the applicant shall pay a license fee for the license, an administrative and investigative fee and such other fees as may be established from time to time by the board of commissioners by resolution adopted in open meeting and kept on file in the office of the county clerk. All applicants shall be furnished a copy of the schedule of fees at the time of application for a license under this article. In addition, all fees and taxes due the state and/or county by the applicant, or upon the property on which the establishment is to be located, must be paid in full at or prior to the time of filing the application for the license.
(b) All licenses granted under this article shall be for a calendar year or the balance thereof and the full license fee shall be paid for a license if the license is issued on or after January 1 but prior to April 1 of such year. Three-fourths of the license fee shall be paid if the license is issued on or after April 1 but prior to July 1, one-half of the license fee shall be paid if the license is issued on or after July 1 but prior to October 1, and one-fourth of the license fee shall be paid if the license is issued on or after October 1 of the calendar year for which the license is issued. The license fee for temporary permits under section 6-105 shall not be adjusted in any case.
(c) Each application for a license under this article shall be accompanied by payment for the full amount of the license fee and applicable investigative and administrative fees. If the applicant is denied a state license, the deposit representing the license fee shall be refunded, but the investigative and administrative fees shall be retained.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
354:
A license issued under this article shall at all times be kept plainly exposed to public view at the place of business for which the license was granted.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
355:
(a) No license under this article shall be transferable, except as otherwise provided in this section.
(b) In case of the death of a licensee who is the sole licensee, the establishment for which the license was issued shall be allowed to continue to sell alcoholic beverages in accordance with the terms of the license for a period of 45 days from the date of death of the licensee or until approval of a new licensee, whichever shall first occur; provided, however, that no sale of alcoholic beverages shall be allowed after the seventh day after the date of death of the licensee until such time as a personal representative of the estate of the deceased licensee, appointed by a probate court of competent jurisdiction, shall have registered with the director of development services on forms prepared by the director. Such personal representative shall be subject to all of the requirements that applied to the deceased licensee, and shall agree in writing to operate the establishment during the interim period in accordance with the terms of the license and the laws of the state and county.
(c) In the case of licenses issued jointly to an entity, if there is a change in control or ownership of the licensee, partnership, corporation or other business entity, then an application for a new license must be filed within seven days. Upon issuance of a new license, the authorization to sell under the previous license shall be revoked by operation of law. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the only change in control of the licensee, partnership, corporation or other business entity is a change in the operating manager, a new license shall not be required. A licensee shall have 45 days to hire a new operating manager and the new operating manager shall, within seven days of being hired, submit a personnel statement in the form prescribed by the director of development services, and submit to a background check.
(d) If there is a change in control or ownership of licensee's entity, and if an application for a new license is filed with the director within seven days of such sale or transfer, the establishment may continue to be operated under the then existing license for a period of 45 days or until a new license is issued or denied, whichever shall occur first.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
356:
A license shall automatically terminate without further action in the event any licensee, for a period of two consecutive months after the license under this article has been issued, ceases to operate the business of selling alcoholic beverages as authorized in the license. If the business operation of selling alcoholic beverages is interrupted as a result of damage to the premises which is being repaired or because the premises are being remodeled, then this section shall not apply to such cessation of operation. If a license is issued for the operation of an establishment in a building which has not yet been completed, the license will not be forfeited unless the licensee fails to begin operations within a period of the earlier of 60 days after a certificate of occupancy is awarded or 180 days from the date of issuance of the license.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
357:
(a) All licenses granted under this article shall expire on December 31 of each year. Licensees who desire to renew their license shall file application with the director of development services on the form provided for renewal of the license for the ensuing year. Applications for renewal must be filed on or before October 31 of each year. If a renewal application is received after October 31, the county cannot assure the applicant that a renewal license will be issued by January 1 and the licensee will have to cease the sale of alcoholic beverages from January 1 until the renewal license is issued. If a license renewal application is received after December 31, such application shall be treated as an application for a new license and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules, regulations and fees for the granting of licenses as if no previous license had been issued.
(b) Any person applying for renewal of a license must pay the license, administrative and investigative fees at the time of filing the application. Failure to pay such fees at that time shall result in the application for renewal being treated as not filed or withdrawn. Any person applying for a renewal license who meets the qualifications of section 6-50 shall be issued a renewed license.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 16-32, § 1, 11-1-2016)
358:
The director of development services, in order to determine if the provisions of this chapter are being complied with or to determine the eligibility of an applicant, may require a licensee or an applicant for a license under this article to provide the director with audited financial statements of the licensee or applicant for such period as the director may determine. The director shall also have the authority to conduct an audit of the books and records of a licensee or an applicant. If the director deems it necessary to conduct such an audit, the director shall so notify the licensee or applicant of the date, time and place of the audit. The director shall designate the person to perform such audit. The licensee shall cooperate with such audit or forfeit all licenses issued under this article. If an applicant for a license fails to cooperate with an audit, the application shall be deemed withdrawn.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
359:
If any person shall fail to pay any sum due under this chapter, the director of development services or his designee shall issue an execution against the delinquent person and his property for the amount of the delinquent fee or tax. No person or entity shall be granted an alcohol license, or have its license renewed, until all monies otherwise owed to the county, including, but not limited to, property taxes, occupation taxes and stormwater fees, shall be paid unless a proper appeal of the same is pending.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
360:
Each licensee shall keep a copy of this chapter, the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code and any regulations issued under such code on the premises. The licensee shall instruct any employee or agent of the licensee working in connection with the sale of alcoholic beverages as to the requirements of all laws and regulations applicable to such sales so that the licensee, his agents and employees selling alcoholic beverages shall at all times be familiar with the requirements of the laws and regulations applicable to such sales. The licensee shall be responsible for any acts of his agents or employees which are in violation of this chapter or of the laws of the state or the rules and regulations of the state revenue commissioner applicable to the sale of alcoholic beverages.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
361:
(a) A license under this article may be suspended or revoked by the board of commissioners when the licensee furnishes fraudulent or untruthful information on the application or any renewal application for a license, or for failure of the licensee to pay all fees, taxes or other charges imposed under the provisions of this chapter or other laws or ordinances of the county or state.
(b) Whenever the state shall revoke or suspend any permit or license to sell alcoholic beverages, the license issued under this article shall be automatically revoked or suspended, as the case may be.
(c) If the director of development services, the board of commissioners or its designated committee believes that probable cause exists to find that a violation of sections 6-6, 6-88 and/or 6-94 has occurred in an establishment operated pursuant to a license under this article, the board of commissioners or its designated committee may temporarily suspend such license pending final determination and action on the matter by the board of commissioners or its designated committee.
(d) The director of development services shall revoke a license under this article where alcoholic beverages have been sold or distributed at the location covered by the license during a period of suspension of such license.
(e) The board of commissioners may suspend or revoke any license under this article when the licensee does not meet the licensing qualifications set forth in this article and such information becomes known to the director of development services or the board of commissioners.
(f) An act or omission of a licensee, its partners, officers, members which constitutes a violation of federal or state law or this chapter will subject the licensee to suspension or revocation of his license when the board of commissioners determines that the act or omission did occur, regardless of whether any criminal prosecution or conviction ensues.
(g) An act or omission of an employee of license on the licensed premises which constitutes a violation of federal or state law or this chapter will subject the licensee to suspension or revocation of his license when the board of commissioners determines that the act or omission did occur, regardless of whether any criminal prosecution or conviction ensues; provided the board of commissioners determines that the acts of the employee were known to or, under reasonable circumstances, should have been known to the licensee, or were condoned by the licensee, or that the licensee had not established reasonable practices or procedures to prevent such act or omission from occurring.
(h) A license under this article may be suspended or revoked whenever the board of commissioners determines that a licensee no longer maintains the responsibility upon which issuance of the license was based or whenever the licensee has defaulted in any obligation of any kind whatsoever lawfully owing to the county.
(i) A license under this article may be suspended or revoked whenever the board of commissioners determines that the establishment operated pursuant to the license has been the scene of repeated incidents of violence resulting in injury to a person or damage to property or a disturbance of the peace or requiring the intervention of law enforcement officers on the scene of a single incident of severe violence resulting in the death of a person or serious injury to a person requiring inpatient hospital care for the injured person.
(j) Upon completion of any period of suspension, a license under this article shall not be reinstated until the licensee has paid the county a reinstatement fee equal to the original license fee for that calendar year. In addition, the licensee shall pay the administrative and investigative fees and update all license application forms.
(k) A license under this article shall be immediately revoked upon a conviction of applicant or any other person required to be named on the application of a violation of any federal, state or local law pertaining to the possession, manufacture, sale or use of alcoholic beverages, controlled substances, or imitation controlled substances.
(l) A license under this article shall be revocable for a criminal charge of any violation of federal, state or local law pertaining to the possession, manufacture, sale or use of alcoholic beverages, controlled substances, or imitation controlled substances which took place at the business establishment for which the license is given.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
362:
(a) Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, or unless waived by the licensee, no license under this article shall be suspended or revoked without the opportunity for a hearing as provided in this section.
(b) The director of development services shall provide written notice to the licensee of the initiation of an action to suspend or revoke a license. Such written notification shall set forth, in reasonable detail, the reasons for such action and shall notify the licensee of the right to a hearing under the provisions of this section. Any licensee against whom action for the suspension or revocation of a license is initiated may have a hearing concerning such action before the board of commissioners or a committee thereof designated by the board of commissioners. Such hearing shall be by written request, filed in the office of the director of development services within seven days after the date of the notice of the initiation of the action from the director of development services to the licensee. Such written request shall set forth the reasons why the licensee feels that the proposed action should not be taken and, in reasonable detail, the grounds and facts which the licensee contends support the licensee's position. The board of commissioners shall determine whether or not the license shall be temporarily suspended during the period prior to the hearing and until action is taken by the board of commissioners or its designated committee. Failure of the licensee to request a hearing within the time specified shall be deemed to be a waiver by the licensee of a right to a hearing, and the board of commissioners shall be authorized to proceed with final action on the matter without the holding of a hearing.
(c) The board of commissioners, by resolution, may assign the duties of conducting a hearing to a committee of the board of commissioners. The committee's action shall be final.
(d) A hearing, if requested, shall be held within 45 days of the date of filing the request for a hearing with the director of development services. At such hearing the licensee shall have the right to be represented by an attorney, at the expense of the licensee, and to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses.
(e) The action of the board of commissioners or its committee shall be forwarded to the director of development services within seven days after the conclusion of the hearing, and the director of development services shall notify the licensee by certified mail, return receipt requested, of the action taken by the board of commissioners or its committee.
(f) The action of the board of commissioners or its committee shall be final when taken.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
363:
For the purpose of this chapter, notice shall be deemed to be delivered when such notice is personally served or, if mailed, it must be mailed to the licensee at the address given in the latest application for the license under this article by certified mail, return receipt requested, and shall be deemed delivered on the third day after the date of deposit in the United States mail.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
367:
(a) A retail consumption dealer which is an indoor commercial recreational establishment shall not sell alcoholic beverages at any time that such dealer is having a promotion or event for which it can reasonably be anticipated that in excess of 50 percent of those persons attending will be under 21 years of age.
(b) An indoor commercial recreational establishment which is a billiard parlor and is operated pursuant to a license shall not admit any customer to the premises who is under 21 years of age at any time that alcoholic beverages are being offered for sale on the premises.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
368:
There shall be no gambling, betting, lotteries, games of chance or the operation of any scheme for hazarding money or any other thing of value on any licensed premises. No retail consumption dealer shall permit in his establishment slot machines, pinball machines or similar machines which require a federal gambling stamp. Notwithstanding anything in this division to the contrary, this section shall not prohibit the sale on the premises of any retail consumption dealer of state lottery tickets, cards or games which are legally sold under the laws of the state.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
369:
(a) Alcoholic beverage sales can be made by a retail consumption dealer in a patio/open area type environment on the premises if the retail consumption dealer has been approved to do so by the director of development services.
(b) To obtain such approval, the patio/open area must be enclosed by a permanent structure providing for public ingress/egress only through the main structure on the premises covered by the license.
(c) The height of the enclosing structure shall be a minimum of four feet above ground level. Such enclosing structure does not have to be solid, nor does it have to restrict visibility into or out of the patio/open sales area. Such enclosing structure must be permitted and approved by development services.
(d) There must be an approved emergency fire exit (not for general public use unless an emergency exists) from the patio/open sales area which should be of the type that sounds an alarm so that the licensee will be alerted in the event of unauthorized use when no emergency exists.
(e) If a licensee desires a patio/open sales area inside an existing structure, plans will be reviewed and approved on an individual basis by the director of development services. Interior-type patio/open sales areas must also meet the requirements of the county's planning, zoning, engineering and fire codes, and any applicable codes of the state.
(f) Notwithstanding anything in this section to the contrary, if the retail consumption dealer is an outdoor commercial recreational establishment, alcoholic beverage sales can be made outdoors in the open, provided that such alcoholic beverages must be consumed on the premises of the outdoor commercial recreational establishment and may not be carried off of such premises.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
370:
(a) Except for the area and circumstances specified in subsection (c), below, and as specified in section 6-117, no person shall leave the building in which alcoholic beverages are sold with open alcoholic beverage containers unless such person is in a patio/open sales area which is approved in accordance with section 6-89 or on the premises of outdoor commercial recreational establishments with an existing license. It is the licensee's responsibility to ensure that no open alcoholic beverage containers are carried out of the building in violation of this section.
(b) People shall not gather outside any building in which alcoholic beverages are sold and consume alcoholic beverages or loiter. It shall be the responsibility of the licensee operating the business in such building to prevent such gatherings.
(c) Within the area of the county bounded on the west by Evans Town Center Blvd, on the north and east by North Belair Road, and on the south by Evans to Locks Road the following regulations apply:
(1) Any licensee may sell alcoholic beverages in a paper or plastic cup for removal from the premises; provided, however, that the alcoholic beverage is not placed in a can, bottle or other glass container and, further provided, that the licensee may sell no more than one alcoholic beverage per person, per transaction, and no person shall remove more than one alcoholic beverage from the premises at a time; and
(2) Any alcoholic beverage dispensed pursuant to this section shall not exceed 16 fluid ounces in size and no person shall possess an open container containing an alcoholic beverage in excess of 16 fluid ounces on the streets, sidewalks, parks, squares or other public places within the area described in this section. No person shall possess more than one alcoholic beverage at a time.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 18-03, § 2(Exh. B), 2-6-2018)
371:
A retail consumption dealer shall not require, permit, suffer, encourage or induce any employee or person to solicit on the premises, for himself or for any person other than the patron and guest of the patron, the purchase by the patron of any drink, whether an alcoholic beverage or nonalcoholic beverage.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
374:
The sale of alcohol shall not be permitted at an adult bookstore, adult entertainment establishment or adult theater as defined in section 90-9 of this Code of Ordinances.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
375:
Officers of the sheriff's department, health department, fire marshal, or code enforcement shall have the authority to inspect an establishment operated pursuant to a license under this article during the hours in which the establishment is open for business. Such inspections shall be made for the purpose of verifying compliance with the requirements of this chapter and state law. This section is not intended to limit the authority of any other county officer to conduct inspections authorized by other provisions of this Code.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
376:
The sheriff or the director of development services, or their designees, may immediately close an establishment operated pursuant to a license under this article in case of an emergency, for the safety of the public or to investigate a crime for a period of time not to exceed 24 hours, or for such longer period of time as law enforcement officials may reasonably require to complete a criminal investigation at the establishment.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
377:
No person shall bring his own alcoholic beverages into any commercial establishment regardless of whether or not such establishment is operated pursuant to a license under this article. For the purposes of this section, the term commercial establishment shall not include a private hotel room or other similar guest room or a private club.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
378:
A license for the sale of distilled spirits by the drink for consumption on the premises will be issued only for an eating establishment, a hotel, an indoor or outdoor commercial recreational establishment, a private club or a on commercial vessel operating or moored in waters located within the county. When eating establishments are located in hotels, shopping malls or high-rise office or apartment buildings, every public entrance to the eating establishment shall be from the outside or a public lobby, hallway, mall or other publicly used interior portion of the primary use structure.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 18-12, § 2, 9-18-2018)
379:
Alcohol may be sold at all times not otherwise prohibited by state law.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
380:
Persons holding a license to sell distilled spirits for consumption on the premises shall not be permitted to make any package sales of alcoholic beverages on such premises.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
381:
Alcoholic beverages must be sold by employees of the licensee within the premises covered by the license.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015; Ord. No. 19-17, § 1(Exh. A), 1-7-2020)
382:
A retail consumption dealer must keep his inventory of alcoholic beverages only on the premises covered by his license.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
383:
No license for the sale of beer or wine for consumption on the premises will be issued except for an eating establishment, a hotel, an indoor or outdoor commercial recreational establishment, or a private club. This section shall not apply with respect to: (1) tastings provided pursuant to a wine or beer tasting permit or (2) tastings provided pursuant to a growler beer tasting permit.
(Ord. No. 15-13, § 1(Exh. A), 5-19-2015)
385:
Functions held in the unincorporated area of Columbia County at which alcoholic beverages are sold or provided will require temporary permits except as set out in subsection (4) below.
(1) Temporary permit required. A temporary permit must be purchased for any function at which alcoholic beverages are sold to the guests directly or indirectly. The individuals, or an officer with authority to bind the entity, putting on the function must apply for the temporary permit. In the alternative, if a Columbia County properly licensed retail consumption dealer or a properly licensed retail consumption dealer in another Georgia County that borders on Columbia County is catering the alcoholic beverages being provided at the off-premises function, the temporary permit may be issued to such retail consumption dealer.

Recomputation of tax; authority to make; basis of recomputation. If the director of development services is not satisfied with the return of the tax or the amount of the tax to be paid to the county by any person, the director may cause an audit of the books and records of the licensee to be performed and may compute and determine the amount required to be paid upon the basis of any information within the director's possession or that may come into the director's possession. It shall be the duty of each licensee subject to the collection or payment of any of the excise taxes set forth in this article to keep and preserve his records relative to the collection and payment of such taxes for three years.
(1) Interest. (3) Penalty for negligence or disregard of rules and regulations. If any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination has been made is due to negligence or disregard of rules and regulations, a penalty of 15 percent of the amount of such deficiency shall be added to the tax.
(4) Penalty for fraud or intent to evade. If any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination is made is due to fraud or an intent to evade any provision of sections 6-151—6-156, or other authorized rules and regulations, a penalty of 25 percent of the deficiency shall be added to such tax.

The notice may be served personally or by mail. If such service is made by mail, such service shall be made pursuant to section 6-63.

Except in the case of fraud, intent to evade the provisions of this article or authorized rules and regulations, or failure to make a return, every notice of a deficiency determination shall be mailed within three years after the twentieth day of every month following the monthly period for which the amount is proposed to be determined, or within three years after the return is filed, whichever period should last expire.

(a) All animals found running at-large in violation of this chapter may be seized or impounded by an animal control officer or any officer empowered to act by law, and detained at the county kennel. The owner of any animal impounded may, within five days after such impoundment, reclaim the animal by the payment of an impoundment fee, plus boarding fee, as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file in the county clerk's office, for each day the animal was impounded. Such action may be taken to control the spread of disease or to eliminate any further pain and suffering of the animal. If the owner is known or can be reasonably ascertained and the circumstances of the situation permit, reasonable attempts should be made to stabilize the animal and to afford the owner the opportunity to pick up the animal.
(Ord. No. 20-03, § 1(Exh. A), 3-17-2020)

Animals shall not be provided to any public or private institution, animal dealer or other individual who may use or supply the animal for research purposes.

(Ord. No. 20-03, § 1(Exh. A), 3-17-2020)
420:

Dogs will only be accepted after showing of proof that it has current vaccinations for rabies, distemper, hepatitis, parainfluenza, parvo virus, and boardatella. Cats will only be accepted after showing of proof that it has current vaccinations for distemper, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, and panleukopenia. (a) A "public nuisance animal" means and includes any animal that meets any of the following criteria:
(1) Is repeatedly found running at-large.
(2) Is found on the property or damages the property of any person other than its owner or keeper without the express consent of such other owner or the occupant of said other property.
(3) Attacks a person or another animal without provocation
(4) Acts in a vicious manner so as to menace any person or other animal.
(5) Excessively makes disturbing noises, including, but not limited to, continued and repeated howling, barking, whining or other utterances causing unreasonable annoyance, disturbance or discomfort to neighbors or others in close proximity to the premises where the animal is kept.
(6) Creates unsanitary conditions or offensive and objectionable odors in enclosures or surroundings, and thereby creates unreasonable annoyances or discomfort to neighbors or others in close proximity to the premises where the animal is kept.
(b) No person shall be charged with violating subsection (c) of this section on the basis of the animal being a public nuisance animal pursuant to subsection (a)(5) of this section unless written warning has previously been issued by an officer authorized to enforce provisions of the Code within 90 days of the charged violation and there are at least two complaining witnesses who shall have signed a written statement stating the address of the animal owner, a description of the animal, the circumstances causing the violation and the date, time and location of the violation. Such complainant shall be required to appear in a court of relevant jurisdiction to address the concern. An animal shall not be deemed a public nuisance animal pursuant to subsection (a)(5) of this section, if at the time a person is trespassing upon the property upon which the animal is kept or any person is on the land adjacent to that on which the animal is kept and is intentionally trying to incite the animal and cause it to make noise or a disturbance.
(c) It is a violation of this section for any person to maintain or keep an animal in such a manner or in such conditions that it is a public nuisance animal or otherwise allow an animal owned or maintained by it to be a public nuisance animal.
(d) A public nuisance animal may be impounded and the owner or keeper of such animal may be charged with a violation of this section and shall be subject to penalties and costs as set forth in section 1-9 of the Code. Each day that a violation of this section continues to exist shall constitute a separate offense.
(e) Complaints concerning animals being kept in violation of chapter 90 of this Code shall be investigated and handled through the county planning department.
(Ord. No. 20-03, § 1(Exh. A), 3-17-2020)

(a) In accordance with rules and regulations promulgated by the county board of health, except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, an animal known to have bitten a person shall be confined in the county kennel or shelter for a period of ten days. (a) No person may abandon an animal. As used in this section "abandonment" is defined as deserting, forsaking, or intending to give up absolutely an animal without securing another owner or without providing the necessities of life. "Necessities of life" includes:
(1) Adequate water which means a constant access to a supply of clean, fresh, and potable water provided in a suitable manner for the species;

497:
(a) Naming.
(1) New roads.
a. New road names submitted by a developer will be reviewed and approved during the plan review process. New road names being initiated by Columbia County will be considered at a scheduled committee meeting with final approval being considered by the board of commissioners.
b. New road names submitted by individual property owners or groups for naming a private easement, private road, private street, private avenue, private lane, private way, or similar private paved, gravel, or dirt thoroughfare will be considered by making application to the agency. Once the application is received, it will be scheduled for the next available committee meeting with final approval considered by the board of commissioners.
(2) Honorary road names.
a. Honorary road names submitted by an individual or group will be considered by making application to the agency. Once the application is received, it will be scheduled for the next available committee meeting with final approval considered by the board of commissioners.
(3) County owned buildings and facilities.
a. The naming of county owned buildings and facilities will be designated by the Columbia County Board of Commissioners by resolution adopted by majority vote.
b. County buildings or facilities being named or given a title will include but not be limited to buildings, areas in buildings, and recreational facilities.
c. Official names belonging to Columbia County, Georgia will remain the same unless changed by the board of commissioners upon relocation or change in function of the building or facility.
d. The naming of county owned buildings and facilities after individuals is discouraged with the following exception:
1. Deceased person(s) who brought honor to Columbia County, Georgia or made a significant monetary or other significant contribution to the development of the county, a county building, or a county facility will be considered. Such monetary gift shall at a minimum have represented 25 percent of the total county commitment of costs as established by the engineering services division.
e. The naming of a building or facility will be effective for the useful life of the building or facility so long as it is used for the purpose for which it was used at the time of the gift. At the end of the useful life of the building or facility and/or the cessation of the use in effect at the time of the gift, Columbia County, Georgia may rename the building or facility.
(b) Procedures.
(1) Roads.
a. The developer shall submit to the agency during the plan review process, the proposed road names to be utilized within the subdivision or commercial development.
b. Agency will notify the developer of the proposed names that are acceptable once the agency has reviewed the proposed names and cross checked them against the current county road index.
c. Agency will only allow the process to be re-initiated twice. If the resubmitted names by the developer are not approvable, agency reserves the right to select from a list of approvable names. The agency will provide a digital file of the official county road index to the developer upon request.
(2) Honorary road names.
a. Applicant shall consult with agency prior to submission of an application for a honorary road name for a road that is county or privately owned.
b. Applicant shall then submit a formal application for the honorary road name. Said application shall include the requested honorary road name and two alternate names accompanied by a petition signed by 100 percent of the affected property owners.
c. The applicant shall pay a non-refundable honorary road naming fee of $250.00 to the agency. Payment of this fee does not in any way guarantee that the honorary road name request will be approved.
d. Once the application is received, it will be scheduled for the next available committee meeting with final approval considered by the board of commissioners.
e. The committee will consider the honorary road name at its next regularly scheduled meeting and submit its recommendation to the board of commissioners for final decision.
f. After final decision of the board of commissioners, if approved, the agency will notify the affected property owners of the status of the honorary road name application. No addresses will be used utilizing the honorary road name. If disapproved, no further action will be taken by the agency.
(3) County owned buildings and facilities.
a. The naming of county owned buildings and facilities will be administered through the office of the county administrator.
b. Proposed name(s) may be submitted on a form provided by the agency. Said form shall provide a detailed background on the proposed name(s) and worthiness of the proposed change.
c. Suggested names will be presented in the form of a resolution to the next committee for consideration at its next available meeting.
d. The resolution will then be forwarded to the full board of commissioners for consideration. Said resolution will require two readings by the board of commissioners.
(Ord. No. 14-01, 7-1-2014)

(a) All properties, lots, and parcels of land shall hereafter be identified by reference to the numbering system adopted herein, except that all existing number identification of buildings or lots or parcels not in conformity with this system shall be changed within (6) months from the adoption of this article so as to conform.
(b) The agency shall invite the involvement of the residents of affected areas in determining modified street numbers by public notice of such intent. However, nothing in this chapter shall be considered to usurp authority of the agency to make final decisions regarding the numbering system, numbers assigned, or compliance with this chapter without public involvement.
(c) Numbers shall be assigned along both sides of the road, with even numbers appearing on the left side of the road and odd numbers appearing on the right side of the road in the ascending direction.
(d) The following criteria shall govern the numbering system:
(1) All number origins shall begin from the intersection of the primary or secondary through or cross street. For dead-end roads or subdivision cul-de-sacs, numbering shall originate at the intersection of the adjacent road and terminate at the dead-end.
(2) The number assigned to the primary structure shall be the same number assigned to the real property in which the structure is situated.
(3) Every structure with more than one principle use or occupancy shall have a separate number for each use or occupancy. For example, duplexes will have two separate numbers.
(4) Apartments will have one property number followed by an apartment number based on the building number and apartment location within the building. For example, following the property number, building number one will be addressed with a one prefixing the apartment number, for example, 475 Belair Road, Apt. 101.
(5) On those streets accessed from either end, the property numbers shall originate from the end of the street carrying the greatest traffic volume.
(6) Notwithstanding the above, streets with the same name continuing into Columbia County from another municipality shall be numbered consistently based on beginning with the next consecutive number following the last number within the other municipality as feasible.
(7) Whenever any residence or other structure is constructed or developed, it shall be the responsibility of the new owner to obtain an assigned number from the agency. An assigned number shall be required prior to issuance of the building permit. In new subdivision developments, no numeric address shall be assigned prior to final plat approval by the Columbia County Planning Commission. Numbers shall be assigned and recorded on the final plat.
(Ord. No. 13-06, 12-3-2013)
505:
(a) Numbers should be displayed as follows:
(1) For single family residential structures, numbers shall be posted using street line posting as described below.
(2) For multi-family residential structures, numbers shall be posted using structure posting as described below.
(3) For commercial structures, numbers shall be posted using both street line posting and structure posting.
(b) All owners of structures shall, within the time-frame stipulated herein, display and maintain the assigned numbers in a conspicuous place on or near said structure in the following manner:
(1) Street line posting: The assigned number shall be displayed on a post, fence, wall, mailbox, or on some other structure with an approximate height of four feet at the property line adjacent to the access drive of the numbered structure. The exact height and location of the posting may vary in order to ensure that the sign remains unobstructed from view. The posted numbers shall be visible from both directions on the road.
(2) Structure posting: The assigned number shall be displayed on the front of the structure within five feet of the front door and visible from the road where practical.
(3) Size and color of numbers: Properties used for residential purposes shall have posted numbers a minimum of three inches high. Commercial properties shall have posted numbers a minimum of four inches high. All numbers shall be a contrasting color to their background. Structure signs and mounting poles meeting these specifications are available for a fee from the Columbia County Fire and Rescue Division Headquarters.
(4) Any number aside from the assigned number shall be removed from the structure, mailbox, post or stanchion, to prevent confusion with the number assigned in conformance with this article. No person, agency, or business shall adopt, assign, display, or cite any number other than that assigned as provided herein for the purpose of designating location of property.
(5) In residential instances where the property is located on a private drive where more than one residence is located, the assigned number must be posted on the main road. It must also be posted adjacent to the access drive of the property using the street line posting.
(6) In situations where a property is located on a private drive and has more than one structure or a structure with more than one principle use or occupancy, numbers should be posted using the structure posting, in addition to the posting requirements of subsection (5), set forth above.
(7) The owner, occupant, or person in charge of any house or building to which a number is assigned or modified shall be notified in writing of that assignment at any time after adoption of this article.
(8) Notices provided herein shall seek to govern or regulate the placing of assigned numbers as prescribed by the United States Postal Service.
